svg.title: Magnetic collar for the DYP L06 sensor
svg.desc: Three panels. Left: the sensor as delivered, side view from the DYP datasheet: a 33.8 millimetre diameter, 4.2 millimetre thick flange that holds the electronics and the cable, with a 17.5 millimetre diameter boss standing 7.9 millimetres off one face, 12.1 millimetres overall. The boss face is the ultrasonic probe and is the side that goes against the tank; the flange is the back. Middle: the printed collar seen from the tank side, 44 millimetres outside diameter, an 18.5 millimetre bore that the boss passes through, three 8 by 3 millimetre magnets in pockets at 120 degrees on a 30 millimetre pitch circle flush with the tank face, and a 4 millimetre cable notch through the back wall. Right: section through the collar on the tank. The collar is 11.8 millimetres thick. A 34.2 millimetre diameter, 4.2 millimetre deep recess in the back face holds the flange; the shoulder between that recess and the bore is 7.6 millimetres thick, so the 7.9 millimetre boss stands 0.3 millimetres proud of the magnet faces. The magnets pull the collar to the steel, the shoulder pushes on the flange, and so the boss face is pressed into a silicone grease film. Dimensions are a starting point to confirm by test fit.
svg.text: Magnetic collar for the DYP L06 (dimensions in mm, starting point: confirm by test fit)
The sensor hangs under the cylinder. In every panel the tank is at the top and "up" means toward the tank.
The sensor (datasheet 1.6)
side view, boss up, 6 px per mm
cable
probe face, dia 17.5: this side goes against the tank
boss 7.9 tall
flange dia 33.8, 4.2 thick
The probe is the raised boss. DYP's own EVA ring goes
over the boss onto the flange face, the couplant goes
on the boss face inside the ring, and that side is
pressed to the steel (installation instruction 5.2 to 5.8).
The flange is the back. It holds the electronics and
the cable and never touches the tank. A collar that
puts the flange against the steel holds the probe
12 mm away from it and cannot read.
Collar, seen from the tank side

magnets 8 x 3 N42-N52, flush, same pole out

Section on the tank

cylinder bottom, steel 2-3 thick
boss (probe)
flange

OD 44
silicone grease film between the boss face and the steel
collar 11.8 thick, tank face to back face
flange recess dia 34.2 x 4.2 deep, open at the back

The magnets pull the collar to the steel. The collar's
shoulder pushes on the flange, so the boss face is pressed
into the grease film first and the magnets stop 0.3 short
of the steel. Off the tank the sensor can only leave the
collar backwards; two dabs of CA on the flange edge stop
that. The cable leaves the flange edge radially, through
the notch cut in the back wall.
Print tank face down (pockets on the bed), 100% infill,
ASA or PETG. Test-fit: the boss slides through the bore
and the flange drops into the recess without force; the
boss face sits just proud of the magnets. Three 8 x 3 N42
magnets at a 0.3-0.5 mm gap pull roughly 1.5 kg: plenty
for a 20 g sensor, the collar and its cable.
Both drawings assume the boss face is flat and the boss is 7.9 tall (12.1 overall minus the 4.2 flange, datasheet 1.6). Measure the real part before printing:
if the boss is domed or a different height, change the shoulder thickness so the face still stands about 0.3 proud.
